content:
After a preview at I/O 2026 in May this year, Gemini for macOS is now rolling out advanced voice control features.

Google positions this feature as letting you "speak naturally in any window on your desktop," offering two main capabilities.

First is smart dictation, which transcribes "spoken words into clean, elegant text." Gemini automatically removes filler words like "um" and "ah," while handling mid-sentence corrections to accurately capture your intended meaning.

The formatted text is inserted at your current cursor position. This provides a voice-to-text experience similar to the upcoming Gboard Rambler on Gemini Intelligence phones.

The other capability goes beyond simple transcription, understanding the context of your current screen to execute complex tasks. This opt-in feature requires you to enable Gemini reasoning in the app's settings.

  • Capture and organize information: highlight local files, images, or documents on your desktop, then tell Gemini directly what you need. For example, you could say: "Read these veterinary documents and email a summary of my dog's medical history to the boarding facility."
  • Write and rewrite text: highlight text anywhere on screen to instantly rewrite, adjust tone, and insert the revised version directly where needed using voice. Try saying: "Rewrite these notes into an executive summary and add a TL;DR at the beginning."
  • Generate and edit images: brainstorm concepts or refine plans by generating images with voice; you can also reference designs on your desktop and request quick modifications. Try saying: "Generate a dark mode version of this illustration."

From anywhere on macOS, simply press and hold the Fn key to activate, or click the new screen-sharing button at the end of the "Ask Gemini" prompt. Gemini will display a floating capsule with a waveform at the bottom of the screen.

Make sure you've updated Gemini for macOS to the latest version (1.88). This new voice feature is rolling out globally to all users, currently supporting English, with more languages "coming soon."
